catalog_quote: The Ibanic languages, Seberuang, Mualang, and Iban (specifically the Iban of the Kapuas River, not the Iban of Sarawak), and other Malayic Dayak languages have undergone several areal adaptations which have altered their phonologies. Most importantly, stress in many of the languages of West Kalimantan is consistently word-final, a feature of most of the Land Dayak languages of the Kapuas River area. Some other changes which are found in this area include reflexes of *R, *u, and *i and are discussed in a bit more detail below. [...] 2.8.2.2 Word-final vowel breaking. As a result of word-final stress and phonetic final vowel lengthening, high vowels in Seberuang and Kapuas River Iban have developed lowered nuclei with high off-glides. In Seberuang, *-i > ey and *-u > ow and in Iban *-i > ɪi̯ and *-u > ʊu̯. The changes are allophonic, and have not resulted in any additional phonemic contra…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Seberuang falls consistently on the final syllable (an areal West Kalimantan/Kapuas feature); the stressed, phonetically lengthened final vowel has caused allophonic breaking of final high vowels (kutu [kutow], tali [taley]).
new_statements.exceptions: None; stress described as 'consistently word-final'. No discussion of schwa, clitics or phrase position.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement made in a comparative-historical dissertation's areal-phonology remarks, based on the author's own elicited wordlist data (citation forms) from a Sepauk speaker; not a dedicated stress section, no acoustic evidence.
new_statements.identity_note: Smith's Seberuang data are his own elicitation from Sepauk (Sepauk tributary of the Kapuas, Sintang Regency), consultant Markus Sintang -- the core Seberuang area, same languoid as sebe1242. The stress remark is framed areally (Ibanic/Malayic Dayak of West Kalimantan, shared with Kapuas Land Dayak) and then applied explicitly to Seberuang and Kapuas River Iban. Glottolog's four 'descriptive' refs for sebe1242 actually describe neighbouring Ibanic varieties (Sekujam, Kumpang, Lebang), not Seberuang itself.
